verdict.rationale: GitCafe has no built-in natural-language command interface of its own. It does run an official MCP server at git.cafe/mcp, which lets AI tools such as Claude and ChatGPT read repositories and, with approval, work on issues and pull requests. It also exposes those MCP tools to WebMCP browser agents and offers agent skills for coding assistants, so natural-language operation works through external AI clients rather than natively. Missing for 10: a native in-product natural-language command interface, evidence of which write actions the MCP tools cover beyond issues and pull requests, and hands-on or independent corroboration that natural-language operation works in practice.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: GitCafe runs an MCP server at `https://git.cafe/mcp`, so AI tools such as Claude and ChatGPT can read repositories and, with your approval, work on issues and pull requests.
In a browser that supports WebMCP, GitCafe pages offer the MCP server's tools to the browser's agent.
Add agent skills to give your coding assistant the same workflow.
